problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $2$nd and $4$th rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st and $3$rd rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st and $3$rd rows of $A$ are $4$ and $-1$, respectively.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the answer is $4+(-1)=3.$
